purpose: Explain I2C BUSY under PWM without losing the first event

sources.finding: Spurious master BERR does not abort the transfer; ST specifies clearing BERR and continuing. Existing ec_poll instead calls ec_finish/reset for BERR. This is a concrete policy mismatch, not proof that BERR was the initial PWM event.
sources.clock_check: Current I2C kernelHSI16 and APB170MHz make ratio10.625; outside the1.5..3 first-byte-stall condition. Standard-mode I2CCLK16MHz exceeds the4MHz minimum.

sources.finding: Separate BUSY/STOP/RXNE waits, error flag processing and abort sequencing are explicit; HAL_BUSY software state must not be confused with the hardware BUSY flag. Our capture records raw ISR and pre-reset state.
Official board examples include I2C_TwoBoards_ComIT/RestartComIT/AdvComIT. A bus-driver example does not by itself qualify EMI immunity in a motor inverter.
Example concerns F407/CMSIS busy state and address/IRQ questions; not the same peripheral/driver. Do not copy its busy wait or address convention to G431.
Held-low SDA can be the target retaining an interrupted byte. That explanation needs simultaneous pre-reset pin evidence; late HIGH/HIGH GPIO snapshots do not establish it.
F1/F4 analog-filter BUSY workaround is often suggested. It must not be treated as a documented G431 erratum or automatically copied.

new_firmware_policy: Capture first boot and first PWM fault before reset; preserve current recovery for diagnostic attribution
